takes.why: Half of their favorite underrated stack — take him in the third round; a healthy best-season Nabers 'does not belong anywhere near there.' ASR renders him 'Neighbors'.
takes.mechanism: Stated reason is ADP mispricing conditional on health, explicitly acknowledged as risk-on ('it is playing with fire'). No usage, scheme, or QB-play evidence offered — the whole case is range-of-outcomes vs draft cost.

takes.why: The stack partner — draft him in the ninth round; the good version of Dart badly outproduces that ADP. ASR renders him 'Jackson Dart'.
takes.mechanism: Same pure ADP-range argument as Nabers: both are priced where the downside is already baked in and the upside is uncapped. Stacking correlation is implied but never argued.

takes.why: One host's standing breakout call, reinforced by the Bears adding another field-stretching weapon.
takes.mechanism: Stated reason is weapon depth: 'Xavier Thomas' (ASR, a 4.28 / 190-lb Bears rookie WR) showing blazing speed gives Chicago a fourth weapon who can burn the field. They explicitly say the speedster himself isn't fantasy-relevant — only the QB effect is.

takes.why: Positive health note — 'looks 100%' per Ben Johnson.
takes.mechanism: Direct coach report on health status; no usage or role claim attached.

takes.why: Explicitly NOT a Jacobs-style situation — 'this will not affect Keenan Allen this year'; don't discount him for the Sunday DWI arrest.
takes.mechanism: Stated legal reasoning via Drew Davenport: he was under 0.08, was in a parked vehicle rather than driving, the case won't resolve until year's end, and the expectation is it gets pled down to something innocuous.

takes.why: He, not DJ Giddens, is the insurance back behind Jonathan Taylor — a direct correction to the assumed handcuff.
takes.mechanism: Stated as a preseason depth-chart read ('it looks like he is the insurance back'), confirmed over Giddens by explicit question. No snap counts cited.

takes.why: Passed over as the Jonathan Taylor handcuff in favor of Seth McGowan.
takes.mechanism: Implicit from the depth-chart read above; no independent evidence given against Giddens.

takes.why: 'Not only does he look like the direct insurance running back to Jeanty, but he looks like a player who might actually get on the field.' Name is ASR-uncertain and the team is inferred from the Jeanty reference ('Gentee').
takes.mechanism: Two separate stated claims: depth-chart position behind Jeanty (contingent value) AND standalone preseason on-field ability (immediate value) — they are asserted, not evidenced with usage numbers.

takes.why: Now looks like the true KC backup RB after the incumbent was waived, and 'has looked fantastic'. ASR only says 'Emmitt in Kansas City' — first name only, identification uncertain.
takes.mechanism: Stated reason is a roster-cut vacancy plus a play-style comp: the back who had been running as the backup got waived, and he runs violently/aggressively with 'hilarious similarities to Isaiah Pacheco at his best.' The comp is stylistic, not statistical.

takes.why: Detroit is willing to go into the season with him as the backup — Dan Campbell said he's comfortable with him. ASR renders it 'Sailors'/'Sailor Jerry'; the hosts themselves had never heard of him.
takes.mechanism: Direct coach quote as the only evidence, which is exactly the 'coach praise' category worth discounting relative to beat-writer usage notes.

takes.why: Rookie RB who 'was looking very good' but was put on short-term IR, so the first four weeks are off the table.
takes.mechanism: Stated as preseason performance interrupted by a transaction; the ASR says 'so he won't miss the first four weeks' which almost certainly should read WILL miss — short-term IR is four games. Treat the direction of that sentence as an ASR error.

takes.why: Remains on PUP to start the season — he is off the board for the opening stretch and the reason Jadarian Price is startable.
takes.mechanism: Roster transaction, stated as fact rather than projection.

takes.why: Unanimously drafted over MarShawn Lloyd in the head-to-head exercise. ASR renders him 'Ramondre'.
takes.mechanism: Stated as a risk-tolerance choice, not a talent gap: he offers known production where Lloyd is 'a complete unknown.' The framing explicitly concedes Lloyd has the higher ceiling.

takes.why: Loses the head-to-head to MarShawn Lloyd — take Lloyd over Pollard.
takes.mechanism: Implicit ceiling argument: the Green Bay starting RB role can be a top-12 fantasy player, and that contingent upside outranks Pollard's known role. No Pollard-specific evidence cited.

takes.why: A reported Eagles reunion is 'on the table' and they react to it as bad news — 'that is nasty' — for the incumbent Philadelphia tight end.
takes.mechanism: Stated as target-competition dilution at TE (Dallas Goedert named in the same breath), asserted by reaction rather than argued.

takes.why: Unretiring is the rare piece of GOOD news before kickoff and is IDP-relevant; the surrounding super-team is not expected to work out.
takes.mechanism: Stated reason for the team-level skepticism is a base rate they cite loosely: the last 20 teams favored by this wide a Super Bowl margin went 0-20, plus age/health risk across Stafford, Davante Adams, Donald and Myles Garrett.

takes.why: Survived the cutdown on a reduced one-year deal — he is still on the roster, which is the only fantasy-relevant part.
takes.mechanism: Contract/roster fact: a $3.5M deal cut to $2.5M as a take-it-or-leave-it at the end of camp. One host reads it as the team having no leverage competition for him, i.e. mild negative signal on his standing.

takes.why: His #1 must-have RB — should be a first-round pick and is going at the end of the second.
takes.mechanism: Signed with the Chiefs for almost $30M with no Pacheco and no Kareem Hunt behind/ahead of him, and KC is signaling a heavier run game with Mahomes coming off a torn ACL, plus possible passing-game usage per camp reports.

takes.why: His #1 must-have TE at an eighth-round price.
takes.mechanism: Has quietly finished top-8 at TE every year of his career and is being drafted behind TEs like Harold Fannin who play in worse offenses with worse QB play.

takes.why: His #1 must-have QB, available in round 9.
takes.mechanism: Won championships last year with 30- and 40-point games, and for the first time since 2023 gets a true X receiver in Mike Evans, who has been top-5 in WR efficiency the last two seasons when on the field; Purdy has averaged a top-12 weekly finish when healthy.

takes.why: His #1 must-have WR and a steal at the end of the second round.
takes.mechanism: Clear-cut WR1 for Drake Maye (best QB of his career) and his target competition drops from DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert to Kayshon Boutte, Romeo Doubs and Demario Douglas.

takes.why: Do not touch him until round 10 or later (pick ~120 in 12-team).
takes.mechanism: Placed on the commissioner's exempt list (Schefter) for an off-field investigation with an alleged video; can't play while listed and a suspension looks likely, though the length is unknown and he could still play part of the season.

takes.why: Add him as the clear Packers RB1 but price him as a 6th-7th round back — do NOT reach in the 4th-5th.
takes.mechanism: Jacobs is off the field, Emanuel Wilson is gone and Lloyd took the bulk of first-team carries while Jacobs was out with a groin injury; but Lloyd has no NFL experience, a two-year injury list (hamstring, ankle sprain, appendicitis, season-ending hamstring), was never a workhorse in college, and the Packers OL and offense around him are thin.

takes.why: Don't spend meaningful FAAB or waiver priority on the new Packers trade acquisition — he's the RB3.
takes.mechanism: Pittsburgh's third-round rookie has busted for them and Green Bay only paid a 2028 sixth-round pick, which signals how little either team values him; Steelers were likely to cut him.

takes.why: He is not the real handcuff to J.K. Dobbins despite the draft capital.
takes.mechanism: His 14 fantasy PPG filling in last year was TD-propped, not earned — 3.4 yards per carry (65th in the NFL) and 34th in yards per touch — and at 200-205 lbs he isn't the red-zone body.

takes.why: Last-RB-on-the-bench stash — he has taken over as the clear McCaffrey handcuff and is available in 93% of leagues.
takes.mechanism: Jordan James (the camp RB2) is still recovering from fractured ribs, Black won the RB2 job in preseason week 2 with pass-protection reps and vision, and McCaffrey is 30, coming off 400+ touches and already dealing with camp tightness; the 2024 precedent is Jordan Mason at 17 PPG / 21 carries / 107 rush yards per game in five McCaffrey-less starts.

takes.why: Add him at his 139th-overall price — he's going after kickers and could see close to a 50-50 split.
takes.mechanism: Beat reports (Zane Dailey) say Montgomery and Marks have been used nearly evenly all camp with all-positive tape and coach-speak; Marks handles two-minute/four-minute work and elite college pass-catching production, and Houston's defense should produce run-positive scripts.

takes.why: Still the lead back, but his workload is being overstated — the camp split is closer to even than people think.
takes.mechanism: Houston has kept the aging veteran on ice in camp to avoid injury while Woody Marks takes near-equal reps; Montgomery's role is secured by trade/contract investment, not by camp separation.

takes.why: Should be added in all leagues — he'll be the goal-line/red-zone back and get double-digit touches for the first month-plus.
takes.mechanism: Rodriguez is winning end-of-game and pass-protection reps over Tank Bigsby in joint practices, is getting the red-zone touches in camp, is reunited with Liam Coen (his 2021 Kentucky coach), and ranks 1st in the NFL in YPC and EPA on carries inside the 5 over the last two seasons with 4th-best success rate.

takes.why: Still a breakout candidate, but the takeover comes around weeks 6-12, not week 1.
takes.mechanism: Rodriguez is ahead on pass protection, end-of-game and red-zone work right now; if Bigsby shows the dynamic/explosive ability he flashed, the offense's volume lets him take the backfield later in the season.

takes.why: Free add in 96% of leagues who is operating as Miami's alpha receiver right now.
takes.mechanism: The entire Dolphins WR room turned over (Waddle traded to Denver, Tyreek gone, Tutu Atwell traded back to the Rams), and in preseason week 2 Douglas was the only WR to play 100% of the starters' snaps (14 of 14) with Malik Willis; camp reports (Omar Kelly, Steve Smith Sr.) call him the top offensive standout.

takes.why: Don't take him as the Dolphins' target-share winner — he has no upside.
takes.mechanism: 65 targets last year produced only 317 yards on a 5.1-yard average depth of target (96th in the NFL) — slot-only usage that would need 6-8 catches a week to matter in PPR.

takes.why: Free-roll add (159th overall / WR59, available in ~75% of leagues) who will start week 1 at X.
takes.mechanism: Cleveland released Cedric Tillman, leaving Boston as the starting X with KC Concepcion in the slot and Jerry Jeudy outside; Matt Harmon's Reception Perception has him at 72% success vs man and 72% vs press with a Pittman/McMillan/Drake London comp family, and a Browns source said 'he looks like he could be Drake London for us.'

takes.why: Undrafted in 90%+ of leagues and he has locked down the Eagles' WR2 job opposite DeVonta Smith.
takes.mechanism: A.J. Brown's vacated role in Philadelphia averaged 131 targets / 85 catches / 1,200+ yards over four years; rookie Makai Lemon missed three weeks with a hamstring and profiles as a slot, and beat reporters plus Jeremy Fowler report Wicks is beating out Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore and Lemon for the two-WR-set outside role.

takes.why: Clear WR2 in Seattle at a 146th-overall / WR56 price — take him around round 11-13.
takes.mechanism: Seattle signed him to a three-year, ~$50M extension after trading a 4th and a 5th for him, added no other receivers, and should throw more than last year's league-fourth-fewest 481 attempts now that the Walker/Charbonnet backfield and Kubiak's system are gone; his Saints usage before the trade was 7.3 targets and ~12 fantasy points per game.

takes.why: Spend almost all your FAAB — he's available in 45% of leagues and should be a round-8-to-10 pick, not a waiver afterthought.
takes.mechanism: 49ers' first pick of round 2 is set to start as the Z (the Aiyuk motion role) with Ricky Pearsall out for the year, Christian Kirk hurt, and Deebo/Kittle/Evans all 30+; he caught 11 passes inside the first 20 minutes of two straight preseason games (first player to do that in 20+ years) and was held out of the finale as a valued starter.

takes.why: He's being pushed down boards to the sixth round and should go in the fourth — buy him, while accepting the injury risk.
takes.mechanism: He's the WR1 in a still-quality Kyle Shanahan offense and the market is overreacting to one camp groin mention from a 33-year-old veteran; the real caveat is hamstring problems in four of his last five seasons.

takes.why: Getting more and more bullish — he's the lead back out of the gate with Charbonnet staying on PUP.
takes.mechanism: Charbonnet remains on PUP to start the season, leaving Price as the lead back mixing with a heavy dose of George Holani — and Holani is an undrafted free agent with roughly 25 career touches, so the competition is negligible.

takes.why: A huge fan — Price is why the Seahawks offense can hold up despite the projected regression.
takes.mechanism: Seattle lost the Charbonnet/Kenneth Walker combo and OC Klint Kubiak's scheme, but the first-round rookie is good enough to carry the backfield.

takes.why: Completely mispriced as WR29 in the 6th-7th round — a lock top-24 WR with a top-12 outcome live.
takes.mechanism: The market is drafting him outside WR2 territory, but his role alongside CeeDee Lamb in a Dallas offense projected 6th in Vegas points per game supports a far higher floor.

takes.why: Worth stacking with Ja'Marr Chase but let him fall — round 4 is the absolute earliest reach, and they'd rather wait.
takes.mechanism: He's usually going in the fifth round, so the stack premium isn't worth a full round of reach; the Bengals are the #1 fantasy scoring environment for them anyway.

takes.why: Doubt he plays week 1 — plan a replacement.
takes.mechanism: Nabers stayed non-committal in his own interview (said people can watch video and think he looks good but he may not be able to run a route without hesitation or be ready to be hit), he's mostly been working to the side in practice, and the Giants have no reason to rush a franchise asset on a non-contender.

takes.why: Lower on him than the market because of the injury return.
takes.mechanism: Buying the injury dip is usually not valuable — players coming back from serious injury (he's 33 and off a torn Achilles, just activated from PUP) are rarely truly 100% even when practice film looks fast.

takes.why: Lower on him than the market for the same injury-return reason.
takes.mechanism: Same rule — coming off a torn ACL, and the practice-looks-good signal overstates readiness.

takes.why: Not a player you can rely on, and probably not ready for week 1.
takes.mechanism: Did not practice Monday with no disclosure on severity, and he has missed significant time in all three of his seasons while only ever being a gadget/backup-to-the-backup with good per-touch efficiency.

takes.why: Out on him as a draft pick — let him prove it in week 1, then chase him hard on waivers.
takes.mechanism: He's missed a lot of the offseason with a setback in early August, the Jets plan to work him in slowly given how much a rookie TE must learn, and unlike the Harold Fannin precedent the Jets already have Garrett Wilson commanding target share (a far better WR1 than Cleveland's was).

takes.why: Split call vs Tee Higgins — one host takes Egbuka on the long view, another takes Higgins now.
takes.mechanism: The toe injury has never officially been confirmed as turf toe, so the pro-Egbuka case is not panicking about the start of the season and playing for the league-winner outcome; the pro-Higgins case is present-tense availability (Higgins is healthy right now even though he's also injury-prone).

takes.why: Worth acquiring — they'd trade MarShawn Lloyd for him in PPR.
takes.mechanism: He got a massive contract and will be an important part of the Colts for several years, with a real case to be the outright WR1, whereas Lloyd is an exciting prospect who has never stayed healthy entering year three.

takes.why: Trade MarShawn Lloyd for Watson 'for sure' in PPR.
takes.mechanism: With Jacobs gone the Packers become more explosive and pass-oriented, so Love and Watson benefit — and Watson's ceiling while upright beats Lloyd's fragile, unproven workload.

takes.why: Likes the consolidated Packers target tree with Golden getting consistent outside opportunity.
takes.mechanism: Green Bay was extremely efficient, is projected to jump from 16th to 9th in Vegas points per game, and losing Jacobs shifts the offense toward explosive plays and more pass volume for the outside receivers.

takes.why: The kind of player you may not be able to start but who always helps the roster reach the end zone.
takes.mechanism: Consolidated Packers target distribution in a Matt LaFleur offense projected to score materially more than last year.

takes.why: Keep betting on him until it finally blows up — he was taken over Chase Brown in a live draft.
takes.mechanism: Baltimore's offense is still Lamar plus Henry even with a weaker offensive line; Lamar's health is the swing factor, not Henry's age.

takes.why: Preferred over Javonte Williams and taken as the Bengals' offensive centerpiece behind Burrow.
takes.mechanism: Explosiveness edge over Javonte Williams, inside the #1 fantasy environment (Bengals, 25.6 Vegas points per game) whose defense should keep games high-scoring.

takes.why: Wait-and-see for week 1.
takes.mechanism: Did not practice with the team on Tuesday and was limited to individual work.

takes.why: If the Jaguars backfield goes to Tuten, that's the better running back.
takes.mechanism: Host has never been an Etienne fan and bets on Tuten being the better player inside a Liam Coen offense that works regardless of personnel.

takes.why: Progressing well toward week 1 but a 50-50 report is not what you want to hear — pair him with his backup.
takes.mechanism: High ankle sprain carries real reinjury risk, so the Cardinals' complementary back (ASR 'Algier', unresolved) becomes close to a must-draft if you take Love, ideally at round 11 or later.

takes.why: He's fine — draft him.
takes.mechanism: Expected to return to full practice next week, which is close to the season but on time for week 1.

takes.why: All in on the Maye–A.J. Brown combination overcoming the schedule-driven regression.
takes.mechanism: New England is Vegas's largest projected regression (2nd in scoring last year, projected 13th) mostly because last year's schedule was easy and this year's is hard — but elite QB play overcomes schedule the way Josh Allen does; the counterargument raised is that Maye's TD efficiency won't repeat and the pass-catching room turned over (lost Diggs and Boutte, added Brown and Doubs).

takes.why: Add him on waivers this week but cap the bid around 60-70% of FAAB rather than emptying the budget.
takes.mechanism: Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner's exempt list with no known return date, and Lloyd has finally stayed healthy through an NFL camp and looks like the week-1 starter over Chris Brooks and the newly acquired Kaleb Johnson.
takes.round_or_adp: somebody I would take in like round six or seven; 60-70% of FAB, not 100%

takes.why: Stash him now, before week 1, as a potential immediate league winner.
takes.mechanism: He is the RB3 on paper but the size/efficiency profile (220+ lb, 1,000-yard college season, 31 catches last year) that would jump R.J. Harvey for early-down and red-zone work if J.K. Dobbins - who has missed 5+ games in each of the last four seasons - goes down.
takes.round_or_adp: available in 70-80% of leagues; would cost 100% of FAB the week after Dobbins goes down

takes.why: Do not treat Harvey as the Denver contingency starter if Dobbins misses time.
takes.mechanism: Harvey lacks the 220+ pound early-down/red-zone profile; he projects to stay the passing-down back while Coleman absorbs the grinder role.

takes.why: Add him as the contingent San Francisco bell cow while he is still free in 80%+ of leagues.
takes.mechanism: He is the clear RB2 behind a 30-year-old Christian McCaffrey coming off 400+ touches, has impressed since returning from a camp injury, pass-protects well, and RB3 Jordan James is still banged up - the same setup that made Jordan Mason a top back for five weeks two years ago.

takes.why: One of the few waiver RBs worth real FAAB right now - add him before week 1.
takes.mechanism: Reports point to a near 50-50 Houston split; Marks is younger, entering year two and by far the better pass catcher, and would inherit a full workload behind an aging, never-explosive David Montgomery on a team whose defense produces leading game scripts.
takes.round_or_adp: available in 63% of leagues (55% available / 45% rostered per Yahoo)

takes.why: His workload is not safe - expect a committee and treat him as a fading asset.
takes.mechanism: He is aging, has never been explosive in his NFL career, and reporting has the backfield near 50-50 with Woody Marks; he holds the red-zone/early-down role only to start the season.

takes.why: His No. 1 waiver RB add - boring, but grab him while he is free in half of all leagues.
takes.mechanism: The last two weeks of camp reporting have him as the short-yardage, red-zone and possibly early-down back, and there is a real chance he leads the backfield in carries to start the year in Liam Coen's offense.
takes.round_or_adp: available in over 50% of leagues (52% as of recording)

takes.why: He can still break out this season, but do not count on him as a week-1 workhorse.
takes.mechanism: Camp has the Jacksonville backfield splitting, with Chris Rodriguez potentially taking the larger early-season share of carries.

takes.why: A last-round pick worth making specifically to park in your IR slot and free a live roster spot.
takes.mechanism: He is on the PUP list and will miss at least the first four weeks, so he occupies an IR slot rather than a bench spot while you add an extra player immediately after the draft.
takes.round_or_adp: last-round pick outside of a defense

takes.why: Free IR-slot stash even if you do not believe in him.
takes.mechanism: He is on the short-term IR/PUP list, so he costs no bench spot, and if Mike Evans gets hurt or De'Zhaun Stribling does not pay off he steps into a top-two role in that offense by week five.

takes.why: Named as a short-term IR/PUP body worth grabbing for a free IR-slot stash.
takes.mechanism: Players on the short-term IR/PUP list consume no bench spot, so rostering them is costless optionality.

takes.why: Stash him now while he is free in 90%+ of leagues; drop him after week 1 if the usage is not there.
takes.mechanism: Miami's post-cutdown receiver room has no proven NFL starter, three of five are rookies, and Douglas has been running as the team's WR1 in camp and the preseason with a 6'4/200+ build and 4.39 speed on back-to-back 800-yard college seasons at a ~20% target share.
takes.round_or_adp: available in over 90% of fantasy leagues

takes.why: His No. 1 week-1 streaming defense - stream it for $1-2 of FAAB.
takes.mechanism: Prime-time divisional matchup against a Giants offense with a new play caller, an inexperienced Jaxson Dart, a questionable Malik Nabers and a third-round rookie or Isaiah Likely as the No. 2 option, against a Dallas defense that has invested heavily (Caleb Downs, an improved defensive line).
takes.round_or_adp: available in over 70% of leagues; 1-2% of FAB or free

takes.why: Second-best week-1 stream behind the Cowboys.
takes.mechanism: They face Carolina, which has one of the worst QB situations in the NFL and a bottom-10 offense where taking away Tetairoa McMillan leaves essentially nothing.

takes.why: Add him now - he is a tier-1 FAAB target he cannot believe is this available.
takes.mechanism: James Conner is on IR and Jeremiyah Love is dealing with a high ankle that may keep him out of week 1, which would leave Allgeier as Arizona's starting running back to open the year.

takes.why: Get him right now; if you cannot stash him, be ready to unload 80-100% of FAAB the moment Saquon misses time.
takes.mechanism: He would instantly become a top-12 fantasy RB because he is a clear No. 1 backup rather than a committee piece, and Saquon Barkley has missed time in multiple seasons with ankle and knee injuries - a tier-1 handcuff in his handcuff rankings.

takes.why: Cheap pre-week-1 stash - keep only if week 1 shows Tennessee is not clear-cut Pollard, otherwise drop him.
takes.mechanism: Tony Pollard should be the RB1, but Spears reportedly had a nice camp and preseason, and week-1 usage is what resolves the split.
takes.round_or_adp: explicitly a lesser FAAB priority than Marks/Allgeier/Bigsby

takes.why: Put him at the top of your buy-low list now and trade for him after an expected week-1 stinker.
takes.mechanism: He draws Houston in week 1 - the best team defense in the NFL at limiting explosive plays and a top-two secondary - and as the outside receiver who beats teams for 20+ yard gains he is exactly what they will take away, while the market still prices him as a borderline top-50 overall player.
takes.round_or_adp: going 51st overall, a fifth-round pick in current drafts

takes.why: Use him as the outgoing piece - flip him after a good week 1 in a softer matchup to buy DJ Moore low.
takes.mechanism: Week-1 matchup asymmetry, not talent: his soft opener versus Moore's Houston draw creates a one-week valuation gap you can arbitrage.
takes.round_or_adp: drafted a couple of rounds later than DJ Moore

takes.why: Sell him into a week-1 spike - a 5-catch, 70-yard game is enough to flip him for DJ Moore.
takes.mechanism: The market overreacts to one week; a modest 12-13 point opener from a popular late pick buys a discounted top-50 asset.

takes.why: Worth a waiver-wire roster spot ahead of your backup QB or TE.
takes.mechanism: He should take a step forward this year and profiles as a clear-cut No. 2 receiver on his own team, i.e. real upside rather than a dead bench slot.

takes.why: A stable-floor flex option worth rostering off waivers, though banged up entering week 1.
takes.mechanism: He has caught 70+ passes from Josh Allen in each of the last two seasons - volume attached to an elite QB.

takes.why: Listed as an upside waiver-wire shot worth taking over a backup QB/TE.
takes.mechanism: Rookie with a lot of hype - a pure upside dart, not a floor play.

takes.why: Fine as a free roster-spot add, but never spend 20-40% of FAAB on him.
takes.mechanism: He is the No. 1 receiver on his own team but his production profile is spike-week driven - last year's 100-yard, multi-TD game with Geno Smith is the archetype of a bid you should not make.
takes.round_or_adp: do not blow 20-40% of FAB on this profile

takes.why: He is generating camp buzz but Sal does not believe in the Baltimore situation for him.
takes.mechanism: Stated as a belief about the offense/target competition, not a measured usage signal - mechanism is thin and should be audited.

takes.why: Drop your backup QB - he was named as the example of the QB2 taking up a bench spot.
takes.mechanism: A QB2 on the bench in a 1-QB league generates zero weekly value while the same slot could hold a contingent starting RB or a high-upside WR.

takes.why: Cut him if you already roster a starting-caliber TE like Tucker Kraft.
takes.mechanism: A TE2 you will never start is a wasted roster spot when 50%+-available running backs are sitting on the wire.

takes.why: Drop him if you already have an early-round TE such as Brock Bowers.
takes.mechanism: Double-tapping the tight end position is a roster-construction error; the second TE should be converted into an RB/WR lottery ticket.

takes.why: Another named TE2 drop candidate if you already roster a decent tight end.
takes.mechanism: Waiver-wire-caliber tight ends are replaceable weekly, so holding one costs you a live RB/WR shot.

takes.why: Watch week-1 Giants backfield usage to decide whether he is a sell-high candidate.
takes.mechanism: Tyrone Tracy and Najee Harris usage in week 1 determines whether Skattebo's role justifies his draft price; the read is a usage check, not a projection.

takes.why: Not interested in him (or Tyrone Tracy) as an add - only as a signal about Skattebo.
takes.mechanism: Stated preference; the only scenario that changes it is week-1 usage showing him seriously involved.

takes.why: Add Miami's third-round rookie now — he is their de facto WR1 and still available in 95% of leagues.
takes.mechanism: Waddle and Hill are both gone; Douglas stood out in camp and lined up as WR1 with the starters in the preseason game.

takes.why: Pick up Cleveland's second-round rookie — locked starter, available in 75% of leagues, heavy rookie target volume.
takes.mechanism: Tillman released leaving Concepcion/Jeudy/Boston as the starting three; a bad defense without Myles Garrett means 500+ pass attempts. MECHANISM AUDIT PASS: this is the trailing-script variant, not the banned thin-backfield one — CLE is a 5.5-win, tier-5 team in team_env, so the volume claim survives the favorite test.

takes.why: Add Wicks (91% available) as a first-month dart — he is about to be Philadelphia's No. 2 receiver.
takes.mechanism: A.J. Brown gone, DeVonta Smith the clear No. 1, rookie slot Makai Lemon behind after hamstring issues all camp; Wicks was extremely efficient as a Packers rookie. SECOND independent Sal flag in six days.

takes.why: Add Shaheed (60% available) — clear No. 2 target behind JSN, and the organization has paid him like it.
takes.mechanism: STATED: a 4th and a 5th traded for him plus a 3yr/$35M+ extension with no other WR added; PLUS 'they should throw more because Walker's gone and Charbonnet's hurt.' MECHANISM AUDIT FAIL on the second half — that is the banned thin-backfield-to-more-passing inference and it is the SECOND time on this same player (first caught 2026-08-24). Seattle is a 10.5-win tier-2 team, i.e. a favorite, and favorites run MORE. The contract/target-competition half stands alone; use that if the conclusion is repeated.

takes.why: His No. 1 add: SF's second-round rookie is a Week 1 starter and still available in 45% of leagues.
takes.mechanism: He sat the third preseason game with the starters (the rest-is-a-signal tell), sits ahead of Demarcus Robinson and an IR'd Christian Kirk, and reports have him used in motion.

takes.why: Trade for Etienne now — a top-30 overall player who just became an unchallenged workhorse; Sal has publicly reversed his own earlier fade.
takes.mechanism: Kamara's sprained MCL costs him a month-plus (third occurrence; one cost six weeks), Devin Neal and Ty Chandler are both on season-ending IR, leaving only Kendre Miller and Audric Estime — none of whom take pass-down work — inside a Kellen Moore offense that runs ~1,100 plays vs a ~1,057 league average.

takes.why: Plan the exit with the entry: sell Etienne before Kamara returns, roughly after week 4.
takes.mechanism: The top-10 window is specifically the weeks Kamara is out; once he is healthy the backfield reverts to the early-down/third-down split the staff described all camp.

takes.why: Buy low aggressively — a borderline top-25 overall player being sold at 5th/6th-round prices over a groin tweak.
takes.mechanism: The injury is minor (2-3 weeks, on track for Week 1); the Jets refused to trade him during a fire sale, extended him 3yr/$45M, and OC Frank Reich volunteered 'Breece Hall is the bellcow'; he produced 1,400 total yards on a 74% backfield opportunity share inside the league's worst passing offense, which Geno Smith should improve.

takes.why: The most slept-on starting RB in the league — and no longer a pure buy-low only because Henderson got hurt.
takes.mechanism: Confirmed RB1 in beat-writer language as of Aug 27, and New England trusted him over Henderson through the playoffs and Super Bowl; a 230-lb three-down/red-zone back who pass-protects better, now with A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and two added offensive linemen.

takes.why: Fade Henderson at his price — he is going a pick AHEAD of the actual RB1 while not practicing.
takes.mechanism: Ten days without practicing on an 'ankle sprain' one week out starts to look like more than a sprain, and even healthy he lost the job back to Stevenson last season.

takes.why: Trade for Mason at his RB38 / round-7-8 price — the bell-cow frontrunner in a better offense than backs going three rounds earlier.
takes.mechanism: Camp reports have him the clear 1A with Aaron Jones isolated to pass work; Jones is 31-going-32 with serial soft-tissue injuries; whenever Mason has had a featured role he has averaged ~16-17 PPG on ~5.0 YPC. MECHANISM AUDIT PASS and notable: the pace half is the CORRECT inverse of the banned chain — a better offense sustains drives and RUNS more. Stated flaw is honest (3/11/14 career receptions).

takes.why: Do not buy Aaron Jones at any price — he is being reduced to a pass-down role.
takes.mechanism: 31-and-a-half, turning 32 in-season, with hamstring injuries in each of the last two seasons plus shoulder, hip and rib issues; a repeating hamstring pattern in an explosiveness-dependent back, and camp reports say the opposite of what they say about Mason.

takes.why: Cheapest buy on the board — a round-9/10 price for genuine league-winning upside.
takes.mechanism: ~900 total yards and 8 TDs as a seventh-round rookie on a broken offense at 4.7 yards per touch (top-25); the groin is minor; and the staff wants him on the field all three downs so the offense has no personnel tell.

takes.why: The stated downside is the Washington offensive line, not the committee.
takes.mechanism: Laremy Tunsil is out effectively all season and the line already fell apart last year; Sal is also skeptical the pass-catching role survives Rachaad White.

takes.why: Buy the top-5 rookie now that he has fallen to round 6-7 on an empty preseason box score.
takes.mechanism: Six targets in ~2.5 quarters is strong usage regardless of zero catches, and the last ten top-10 drafted WRs produced nearly identical preseason lines (Marvin Harrison caught nothing); 7-of-12 for 2 TDs in joint practices; Daboll historically funnels 150-170 targets to a designated WR1.

takes.why: Do not price his 140-target Giants seasons forward — he is a slot receiver here, not the Daboll WR1.
takes.mechanism: His New York volume was forced by everyone else getting hurt in an extremely high-play season; in Tennessee he projects to the slot with a top-5 pick installed at X.

takes.why: Go get Nabers from anyone panicking about his Week 1 status — he plays, and he is a top-10 receiver.
takes.mechanism: He shed the red non-contact jersey ~3 weeks out and has practiced a month, ten months post-ACL; the 'won't commit' quote is communications control and divisional gamesmanship, not a health signal; a ~40% rookie target share and ~44% first-read rate survive a QB20-caliber Dart.

takes.why: Buy Evans at his round-6 price (or right after a Week 1 absence) — the clear WR1 and red-zone alpha in San Francisco.
takes.mechanism: Cooks gone, Kirk on IR, Pearsall out for the year, leaving a 30-plus Deebo and a second-round rookie; the groin/adductor is reported minor with a Week 1 plan; Adams and Keenan Allen both drew 100+ targets at the same age.

takes.why: Pay up now — after one good Week 1 he becomes a second-round rest-of-season asset and the window closes.
takes.mechanism: The down year was injury-segmented, not decline (17.5 PPG on 9 targets across the six games he and Herbert were both healthy); Keenan Allen's 120+ targets vacated with no real replacement; and new play-caller Mike McDaniel plans to use him the way he used Tyreek Hill.

takes.why: Rice is a slam-dunk third-round value and people are panic-selling him — buy.
takes.mechanism: The 'sluggish' clips are half-speed camp reps; he led the NFL with a 46.2% red-zone target share and a 55% designed-target rate while finishing top-5 in PPG over eight games; markets price him at 95.5-99.5 receptions and his target competition is unchanged.

takes.why: Treat Kelce as a sell/downgrade — Sal uses him repeatedly as the throw-in he is happy to trade away.
takes.mechanism: Turning 37, and 'we haven't seen prime Travis Kelce in three years'; he is listed as diminished target competition for Rice rather than as a threat.

takes.why: Deebo will not be San Francisco's WR1 at this point in his career.
takes.mechanism: 30-plus, injured last year and 'looked slow' — a specific problem for a player whose game is built on explosiveness.

takes.why: Below ADP (they rank him 25-26 vs WR22 ADP) but the whole room is afraid to be wrong — upside is a top-10 WR, and if you draft him, stack him with Josh Allen.
takes.mechanism: Stefon Diggs 2020 template: a good WR who never had a great QB becomes the uncontested WR1 for Allen, with Joe Brady scheming him back to slants/crossers/screens (only 21% of his routes last year). Counterweight: age 29 and he stopped breaking tackles in 2025.

takes.why: At/slightly above ADP but the take Mike is most afraid of — he doubts anything on the Giants offense works early.
takes.mechanism: Dart holds the ball, extends plays and runs recklessly — he was in the injury tent in half his starts last year and again this preseason; layered on a Nabers absence and a week-2 pass-rush gauntlet.

takes.why: Raising his risk rating (still drafting him at the price) because the environment is degrading, not because the rushing upside is gone.
takes.mechanism: Three stacked negatives: a beat report calling this the worst Commanders offense in years with an 'inoperable' line; a first-time play-caller replacing Kingsbury and moving under center; and a top-two WR room of two 30-plus receivers. No team has had two 30-plus WRs finish 1-2 in receptions since 2010.

takes.why: None of the three hosts has drafted Barkley anywhere — they take Chase Brown or Kenneth Walker over him at the same price every time.
takes.mechanism: The breakaway runs disappeared until the very end of last season; the market is paying for the RB1-overall memory. Acknowledged bull case: 13 carries inside the 5 for one rushing TD is real positive TD regression.

takes.why: Jason and Mike are OUT at the price everywhere; Andy dissents and took him a round later.
takes.mechanism: Price, not talent: an ACL return with reported first-half snap-count management, priced as if healthy. 'If the ACL got me a 10th-round pick I would do that.' Reported plan is a snap count for the first half of the season, then unleashed.

takes.why: OUT despite Todd Bowles saying he is hopeful for Week 1 — 'he's a bummer' — and they expect his ADP to drop.
takes.mechanism: Four stacked actuarial reasons: turf toe takes longer than expected, it recurs, production is degraded during the recovery window even when active, and Egbuka specifically played poorly through injuries last year. Nuance: Tampa says toe SPRAIN not turf toe, but turf toe IS a sprain of the big toe — the real question is which toe, and he is still working to cut on it.

takes.why: Afraid the market has flipped Brian Thomas and Parker Washington completely upside down.
takes.mechanism: Past success is the best predictor of future success — a top-10 fantasy WR as a first-round rookie with nothing about his health changed; the re-rating is narrative flow toward Parker Washington. Counter used to pass on him: a minimal route tree, big plays and nothing else.

takes.why: So universally called as a breakout that FF treat him as consensus, not a bold prediction.
takes.mechanism: Crowding — 3rd round of a $100k buy-in league and the most-repeated Foot Clan bold prediction; the stated tiebreak against him was environment.

takes.why: Drafted slightly ahead of ADP over Parker Washington; expected to outkick his price.
takes.mechanism: Target security plus red-zone role: 16.8 fantasy PPG in games with 7+ targets, and trust in Brissett to feed him — taken DESPITE the environment (Arizona projects third-to-last in points), so role overruled environment.

takes.why: 'An absolute world' where everyone looks like an idiot for not taking him in the top eight picks — possibly a better talent than Bijan.
takes.mechanism: Elite prospect grade (the Felix model ranks him 3rd all-time behind Gibbs and Elliott) plus a receiving-volume script on a bad team that trails, with Conner not healthy. Precedent: Allgeier never stopped Bijan, so a committee body is not a blocker.

takes.why: A fantasy-MVP pick and an early reach two rounds ahead of ADP — a first-round rookie RB on a top-tier offense whose printed ADP will not survive real drafts.
takes.mechanism: Draft capital plus a cleared path: Charbonnet on IR and slow-played on return, leaving George Holani; Macdonald says nobody on his championship defense has covered Price in practice. His discount exists only because he played behind Jeremiyah Love in college.

takes.why: Fantasy MVP pick: RB26 ADP against their own RB21 consensus, in a Liam Coen offense they expect to be high-powered.
takes.mechanism: Short-yardage trust plus speed, not efficiency: his 3.7 YPC is an artifact of 25% of carries coming in short yardage, where he ranked 5th among all RBs in rush success rate and turned 7 inside-the-5 carries into 5 TDs; he also clears the 11%-of-team-receptions college threshold. Risk acknowledged: a genuinely ambiguous backfield, and Coen's Tampa usage fed a clear No. 2.

takes.why: Fantasy MVP pick: the highest-paid free-agent receiver in NFL history going as WR23, practicing for Week 1.
takes.mechanism: Room consolidation plus contract as revealed belief — Pittman departed, Pierce got $114M, and the one-trick-deep-threat claim is false (55% of routes were digs/ins/crossers/gos). Screen used: of every 1,000-yard receiver in five years, only players aged 32-34 and a just-traded WR were drafted later the next season.

takes.why: Last year's WR9 going as WR25 at the back of the 5th — and one host is 'completely turned around' on him.
takes.mechanism: Two channels: role change (Dan Campbell took over play-calling and deliberately expanded him beyond the deep-ball role) and environment (Detroit is 3rd in average implied team total and favored in 14 of 17 games with a weak secondary). Support: 2+ YPRR in back-to-back seasons.

takes.why: A fantasy-MVP pick — 'going to score the most points of any tight end this season' — and FF have 'no notes.'
takes.mechanism: Route-level usage that ended his rookie year at a TE1-overall rate (31% target-per-route and 2.34 YPRR over the final five games on 81% of dropbacks), plus scheme: Ben Johnson leans on 12/13 personnel and moving Burden into DJ Moore's role leaves Loveland as the de facto slot.

takes.why: A fantasy-MVP pick, and the groin injury has made him draftable again — WR26 after going inside the top 20 a month ago.
takes.mechanism: Scheme fit for YAC creation: 98th-percentile avoided tackles per reception in college, already translated to the 3rd-best rookie YPRR of any wideout since 2011. FF's own caveat: it all rests on Caleb Williams leveling up, and Bears bets are historically bad bets.

takes.why: A fantasy-MVP pick, but FF are split — one would take him around pick 7 rather than 4.
takes.mechanism: The case is monopoly volume and offensive dependence (top-3 in 3 of the last 4 semi-healthy years); the discount is not the injury but perceived loss of explosiveness plus 'San Francisco vibes.'

takes.why: A fantasy-MVP pick and a 2nd-round WR ranked ahead of Justin Jefferson and Drake London, with a genuine WR1-overall range.
takes.mechanism: Volume transfer plus QB upgrade: he moves from a 3,400-yard passing offense to a 4,400-yard one with Diggs' targets vacated, and Drake May throws 10+ yards downfield at the 5th-highest rate while leading all QBs in completion rate, success rate and passer rating on those throws. Age answered with the age-29-30 elite-WR-changes-teams precedent list.

takes.why: A fantasy-MVP pick and a my-guy — 'every piece of Hampton this year.'
takes.mechanism: Scheme-runner fit: McDaniel wants his backs outside the tackles and Hampton went 5.5 YPC there last year, tied for the league lead in EPA per carry outside the tackles behind a bad line.

takes.why: Owned in dynasty and not being started — his health is the open question, and he is not seen as a threat to Hampton.
takes.mechanism: McDaniel's stated willingness to run a lead back into the ground (Achane at 238 carries) means the pass-catching carve-out that would give Mitchell value is exactly what McDaniel does not reliably concede.

takes.why: A fantasy-MVP pick and a last-round shot — a pre-injury first-round talent available at the end of home-league drafts with a path past 100 targets.
takes.mechanism: Empty depth chart plus negative game script: Miami has nobody else to throw to and will be trailing. MECHANISM AUDIT PASS — this is the trailing-script variant on a genuinely bad team (Miami 7-10, post-regime-change), not the banned thin-backfield inference.

takes.why: Preferred to Chris Bell for the first month, with 75%+ snaps expected in September.
takes.mechanism: Availability over talent: Bell missed all of training camp and gets worked in slowly off the knee, while Douglas was drafted ahead of him and has been great all offseason. Room disagreement on record — another host passed on Douglas for Michael Pittman citing the day-2/3 rookie-WR base rate.

takes.why: Table-banged as the third-best all-around RB in football and worth a late first-round pick.
takes.mechanism: Talent and consistency independent of environment — the most consistent RB in football last year with a checkdown-happy, bad QB; the market is fading the Miami offense, not the player.

takes.why: Do NOT start him Week 1 even if active — while still believing he is the primary back by the second half.
takes.mechanism: Availability and role, not talent: no practice since Aug 24, the opener is on a Wednesday with no extra runway, pre-injury reports already had Stevenson leading, and Henderson's pass-protection deficiency is what keeps a rookie off the field against the defending champs.

takes.why: 'Top of season Rhamondre is a steal' — ugly but genuinely productive early-season volume.
takes.mechanism: Direct beneficiary of Henderson's ankle plus the pre-existing coach-trust ordering. Cost-anchored: they would rather guarantee a Week-1 starter than take Judkins, Bucky Irving or David Montgomery in the same band.

takes.why: Active in Australia but start-at-your-own-risk in Week 1; they would start Juwan Johnson or Hunter Henry over him.
takes.mechanism: Snap-count management off the Achilles — the beat says he won't be near his usual 95% share. Counter carve-out: if reports say he plays in the red zone, a 3-17-2 line is live, so hunt red-zone usage, not total snaps.

takes.why: No longer a comfortable top-4 pick — one host now takes him behind McCaffrey, St. Brown and JSN.
takes.mechanism: Unresolved off-field risk with a season-ending tail: still under NFL review, a new video surfaced, and the tell they weight most is that the Rams have not extended a receiver of that caliber. Unlike a late-round suspension risk, a first-round hit is unrecoverable.

takes.why: Very bullish at his 4.10/5.01 price, but the 2-3 turn is a smidge too high — take DeVonta Smith or George Pickens there instead.
takes.mechanism: Pure price arbitrage with the offense as the discount: at the turn you are choosing him over receivers on better offenses with better QBs; two rounds later the same player is outrageous value.

takes.why: Burrow in the 6th is 'outrageous' value, especially as a two-stack with Tee Higgins.
takes.mechanism: Market drift — elite QBs are going later than their production warrants this year, so the edge is procedural: keep flipping to the QB tab mid-draft instead of executing a fixed positional plan.

takes.why: 'Swift is a great pick right now' — expected to be a steal specifically in the early season.
takes.mechanism: Vacated early-season workload (Monangai week-to-week with a knee and effectively out for Week 1) layered on Swift's pass-catching role in a Ben Johnson offense; Roschon Johnson is the named next man up. Health note: the Thursday exit was a cramp, and he is fine for Week 1.

takes.why: A live threat to Bijan Robinson's touchdown ceiling — The Athletic reports managers won't like how many goal-line carries he gets.
takes.mechanism: A prototypical 225-lb bruiser inheriting a role Atlanta has used before: Tyler Allgeier took 19 carries inside the 10 last year, and they do not expect that number to fall much.

takes.why: Unanimous 1.01 and now 'in a tier of his own' after Isaiah Pacheco went to IR.
takes.mechanism: Monopoly workload with no goal-line competitor — Detroit did not sign Kareem Hunt after his visit and endorsed a backup with no track record, so the backfield share consolidates.

takes.why: Would not draft him over Cam Skattebo or Bucky Irving at the 4-5 turn, but price him NOW before someone else does.
takes.mechanism: Contingent workload with a fragility discount — Jacobs is unavailable but Lloyd is 'a super fragile guy,' Kendre Miller keeps leaving practice, and Green Bay added Kaleb Johnson. Do not pay a bell-cow price for an unproven inheritor.

takes.why: Taken as an RB2 in the 6th on the belief he is Denver's lead back at least to start the year.
takes.mechanism: Depth-chart read with a named threat: Jonah Coleman is scarier than RJ Harvey as the eventual usurper, but neither displaces Dobbins in September.

takes.why: An RB3, not an RB2 — the risk read is getting worse even though they rate him well above the rest of the room.
takes.mechanism: Coaching and opportunity, not talent or the injury: they suspect the staff does not love him and that the Giants will rotate. The 'considered retiring' headline is explicitly discounted as context-free clickbait.

takes.why: One host refuses to draft him at all; another will take him at the 4-5 turn while calling him 'a fascinating story.'
takes.mechanism: Role erosion — every camp and preseason report has Kenny Gainwell taking the passing work while Irving handles primary rushing, which caps the PPR ceiling that made him valuable.

takes.why: A 50-50 Week-1 split with Chuba Hubbard getting the first carry, and a hot-hand committee all season — neither back is countable.
takes.mechanism: Health plus precedent: one healthy season since high school and already missing practice with 'general soreness'; last year's Carolina backfield resolved into a week-to-week hot hand.

takes.why: 'A WR1 that nobody wants to touch' in the 8th round — preferred over Josh Jacobs at that price.
takes.mechanism: A coaching/scheme change fixing a borderline-unplayable Rodgers-era season. Counter named on air: Michael Pittman joining the room is a negative.

takes.why: 'More and more bullish' at the 4-5 turn.
takes.mechanism: NO STATED MECHANISM — conviction without a testable channel; the only named risk is age-related injury recovery. Treat as unsupported opinion.

takes.why: The new three-year, $47M-guaranteed extension is a real commitment signal, but usage is still the open question.
takes.mechanism: Contract as revealed belief — the money slots below Zay Flowers and Alec Pierce but is real; the counter is that he has been good yet unused, so the money does not yet prove volume.

takes.why: He was on the whiteboard as an intended third 'my guy' all offseason before the slot went elsewhere — a previously unstated positive signal.
takes.mechanism: Not argued on air; recorded as a conviction signal from their rationed my-guy process, not as a case.

takes.why: Stashed on IR in the 9th and not expected to survive the turn — an IR-slot stash, not a Week-1 asset.
takes.mechanism: The IR-slot conversion play: an injured rookie occupying a reserve slot costs no bench spot, so the pick is free optionality on his return.

takes.why: Taken as a 10th-round veteran over Caleb Douglas, going 'with the data' rather than the rookie.
takes.mechanism: Two base rates applied against a rookie: Douglas was not a first-round WR, and Miami is not a good offense. Live negative: Pittman has been hurt most of camp and Rodgers sounded frustrated about the lost reps.

takes.why: Taken in the 10th explicitly as a hedge against their own Tuten conviction.
takes.mechanism: Ambiguous-backfield insurance: at a 10th-round cost you buy the other half of a backfield you have already invested in, so being wrong about the split costs nothing.

takes.why: Sal starts Gibbs as his biggest Week-1 edge and calls a 22-point platform projection too low; Gibbs is 'in a tier of his own' with 35-40 point weeks coming.
takes.mechanism: Bell-cow workload plus touchdown volume on a top offense; Sal thinks he can rival the McCaffrey/LaDainian Tomlinson best-ever seasons.

takes.why: Locked into Sal's RB2 slot for Week 1 (one of his first three picks).
takes.mechanism: Volume RB on Sal's roster; groin injury trending toward playing per FF news.

takes.why: Slight Week-1 edge to Lamar over Jayden Daniels; both projected 20-25 points.
takes.mechanism: New offensive system and a more proven player; QB is a wash in 1QB formats.

takes.why: Sal starts Daniels (7th-round pick) and expects 20-25 points, a wash vs Lamar.
takes.mechanism: Rushing QB floor; Sal deprioritizes QB in 1QB leagues.

takes.why: Called 'solid' as an opponent's RB starter; not a fade, just no ceiling.
takes.mechanism: Steady lead-back role in Dallas.

takes.why: Sal expects only 8-10 touches in Week 1 and calls his 4th-round ADP 'gross'; a 6th-7th-round breakout price was fair.
takes.mechanism: Minor injury plus camp reports of a 1:1 rep split with Chris Rodriguez, so he may not even be the Week-1 starter.

takes.why: Elite WR1, obvious start Wednesday night.
takes.mechanism: Target dominance; first-round pick.

takes.why: Sal calls London a bad 2nd-round pick and would trade him for George Pickens, A.J. Brown or Justin Jefferson; a bottom-5 offense could turn a 2nd-round pick into 5th-round value.
takes.mechanism: Tua Tagovailoa (named the Week-1 starter) 'has not been good' for two years and looked terrible in camp/preseason; a cratered offense sinks even a 30%-target-share WR, as ARI showed in 2025.

takes.why: Sal wouldn't be shocked if Evans outscores Drake London on Thursday night, possibly with two touchdowns.
takes.mechanism: Reportedly healthy (camp injuries minor, no games missed) and the 49ers' clear No. 1 red-zone option.

takes.why: Evans is an 'almost certainly start' auto-start in the Thursday LAR-SF game if healthy.
takes.mechanism: Evans said at the podium none of his camp issues would have kept him off the field; touchdown upside in a 48.5-total game.

takes.why: In Sal's Week-1 WR slot; he concedes London probably outscores him but isn't sure it's guaranteed.
takes.mechanism: Placed in the WR slot (not flex) for lineup flexibility; volume WR1 in Pittsburgh.

takes.why: Sal is bidding 7-10% of FAAB on a dropped Mark Andrews, calling him 'the best available tight end, not even close' and a sneaky very good TE this year.
takes.mechanism: Not old (younger than Kelce), new offense, best red-zone weapon on the team with Isaiah Likely gone.

takes.why: Andy drafted Andrews as his TE in two of five leagues and thinks he is 'completely left for dead'; Mike and Jason are skeptical (looks slower on film) and would rather have Kelce rest-of-season.
takes.mechanism: 31 years old with a TE age curve that tolerates 31-33, extended by BAL, new scheme, Likely gone, and Lamar still looks for him in the red zone: 10-TD upside.

takes.why: Sal rates Goedert vs Andrews a dead-even coin flip (both 10.6 in his projections) and would take Goedert by a hair if choosing.
takes.mechanism: Best red-zone weapon on his team now that A.J. Brown is gone, new offensive system reported to be better.

takes.why: Sal's fallback TE starter if the Andrews claim fails.
takes.mechanism: Startable TE on a Liam Coen offense.

takes.why: Sal flexes McLaurin (4pm kickoff) and says he 'sweeps the floor' vs Josh Downs.
takes.mechanism: Team WR1 with Jayden Daniels.

takes.why: Sal flexes Nabers (SNF vs DAL) expecting him to play at 70-80% and still dominate Jonathan Brooks; Jayden Reed is his contingency.
takes.mechanism: Questionable tag looks like gamesmanship against a rival in prime time; ESPN says he's good to go.

takes.why: Yahoo's 12.2-point projection is 'comical'; Downs is at best the 3rd and maybe 4th passing option in Indianapolis.
takes.mechanism: Behind healthy Tyler Warren and Alec Pierce, plus veteran Keenan Allen, on a run-first team with a QB coming off an Achilles.

takes.why: 'One of the worst picks in fantasy drafts'; Sal would trade him for Sutton, Montgomery, Kittle, Lloyd, Carnell Tate, Godwin, Addison, Stribling or Odunze, and projects ~10 touches in Week 1 with Chuba leading.
takes.mechanism: Back-to-back ACL tears (no NFL RB has come back productive from that), only 12 career touches, Chuba Hubbard is the extended veteran RB1, bottom-10 scoring offense invites stacked boxes, and the team won't disclose where his 'soreness' is (Sal reads it as the knee).

takes.why: Chuba is 'easily ahead' in Week-1 rankings and the RB1 whether Brooks is healthy or not.
takes.mechanism: Veteran on a two-year-old extension, back from his hamstring and practicing a week-plus; Brooks is limited.

takes.why: Jason: 'I am terrified of Jonathan Brooks' — any bad-looking practice clip makes him want to be 'Chuba for life'; Andy still lists Brooks among insurance backs with standalone Week-1 value.
takes.mechanism: Worked to the side at practice again Monday with 'general soreness' after two ACLs.

takes.why: 'Definitely a breakout player' Sal likes, but unproven and not scary in a Week-1 flex; he 'might' be the Packers' WR1 (Sal doubts it).
takes.mechanism: Vegas prop market has his Week-1 receptions O/U at only 3; thin GB WR room gives him a path.

takes.why: 'Decent' second flex at best; Sal would start Jayden Reed over him.
takes.mechanism: May only be a starter in three-WR sets for the Commanders.

takes.why: Sal's Nabers contingency; he favors Reed over Golden, Diggs and Brooks in Week 1.
takes.mechanism: Established Packers target earner.

takes.why: One of Jynxzi's 'best picks' as a late handcuff RB.
takes.mechanism: Handcuff with contingent value.

takes.why: Named among high-end insurance backs to roster; Andy would rather hold Bigsby than a pure handcuff like Ollie Gordon.
takes.mechanism: Has looked fantastic for Philadelphia on his touches.

takes.why: Jason sees a 60-40 (maybe 65-35) split with David Montgomery that makes Marks startable in some formats; only 59% rostered.
takes.mechanism: Team has said 50-50; Marks looked better than Montgomery in preseason and year-2 players improve.

takes.why: Andy's last-round pick in 'tons of leagues' and the late pick he most wants to watch; Thursday night decides whether he's held or punted to waivers.
takes.mechanism: Year-2, 2nd-round pick, 93rd-percentile athleticism score; question is whether he is the third pass catcher with enough snaps to matter.

takes.why: Sal calls Fairbairn the best fantasy kicker, above Brandon Aubrey.
takes.mechanism: Houston's offense is mediocre and goes for it on 4th down less, so it settles for more 40-60 yard field goals.

takes.why: Avoid Bates (and the Rams' kicker) even though they're good kickers.
takes.mechanism: Detroit and LAR go for it on 4th down and score TDs, yielding extra points instead of long field goals.

takes.why: Sal prefers the Steelers over the Broncos in Week 1.
takes.mechanism: Very good defense at home vs Tua Tagovailoa: 'feels like maybe a pick six'.

takes.why: Very good defense at home on MNF, but Sal would rather face Tua than Mahomes.
takes.mechanism: Matchup vs the best QB of the generation caps turnover upside.

takes.why: Sell Lloyd if you can get Waddle, Odunze, Marvin Harrison Jr. or Christian Watson (real recent comps); fine to hold if he cost a 10th-13th round pick.
takes.mechanism: Nine career NFL touches, repeated hamstring/ankle injuries, never a full college workload (116-carry career high), GB O-line consensus rank 29th, and Jacobs likely returns mid-season.

takes.why: Drafting Lloyd is a bet on whether he's good; if he is over Jacobs' six-plus missed games, he stays involved after Jacobs returns. Jason ranks Jadarian Price only a couple spots ahead of Lloyd for Week 1.
takes.mechanism: Jacobs misses at least six games; a productive fill-in keeps a share of the room.

takes.why: RB3 at best in Green Bay, though he'd pass Chris Brooks for RB2 if Lloyd got hurt.
takes.mechanism: Acquired for only a 2028 6th-round pick (would have been cut) and lacks reps in the offense.

takes.why: Packers backfield is 'one to watch'; Brooks named as the late-round piece of it.
takes.mechanism: Depth behind Lloyd with Jacobs out.

takes.why: Andy and Mike would drop Tank Bigsby or Emmitt Johnson to stash Jacobs; Jason wouldn't bother.
takes.mechanism: Court date moved up to Sept 10 implies a fast resolution and a second-half return, when he'll be very good; caveat that an exempt-list player can't go on IR and burns a bench spot.

takes.why: Sal has him as his highest-ranked Jaguars WR but would trade him for Garrett Wilson, Davante Adams, Rome Odunze or (for RB need) David Montgomery because the market is 'so hot'.
takes.mechanism: Camp hype pushed a 5th-6th round price onto an 18% target-share player; Meyers led JAX in target share in the second half, Brian Thomas Jr. should bounce back, and any injury sends snaps to Travis Hunter rather than to Washington.

takes.why: 'Really good' and likely heavily involved week to week.
takes.mechanism: Led the Jaguars in target share over the second half of last season.

takes.why: Due for a bounce-back year; Sal takes Thomas 1-for-1 over Alec Pierce.
takes.mechanism: Early-season wrist injury explained last year; year two in the Liam Coen offense puts him in better positions.

takes.why: Was breaking out before his knee injury; would absorb offensive snaps if a JAX WR gets hurt or if he struggles on defense.
takes.mechanism: Mostly a DB in camp, but the team's first lever when the WR room thins.

takes.why: 'Maybe Kyle Pitts gets a bigger role' under Kevin Stefanski.
takes.mechanism: Stefanski's tight ends (Fannin, Njoku) took on a bigger share in Cleveland, though he never had a Drake London there.

takes.why: Sal would move Skattebo 1-for-1 for Jeremiyah Love, De'Von Achane (people scared by turf toe) or Bucky Irving; he was never in because he prefers the WRs in his 3rd-4th round range.
takes.mechanism: Najee Harris signing (Harbaugh trusts him for ~8 carries a game, dropping Skattebo from ~16 to 10-12), new regime with no attachment to a 4th-round pick, serious injury recovery (Tony Pollard said it affected him all the next year), and Tyrone Tracy's pass-catching role.

takes.why: Could carve out ~8 carries a game from Skattebo; not the same back after the Achilles but trusted by Harbaugh.
takes.mechanism: 28 years old off an Achilles tear, no guaranteed money, looked decent in the final preseason game, pass-protection role.

takes.why: Might still be involved as an explosive pass catcher despite a blown block and shaky standing.
takes.mechanism: Averaged 99 total yards and 14 fantasy points per game from Week 11 on last year when Skattebo was hurt.

takes.why: Jason drafted him in the League of Record and again the next day: 'Bucky Irving is going to be so good'; goal-line work stays with Bucky.
takes.mechanism: 24 years old, shoulder injury fully behind him, last player of his tier on the board.

takes.why: Sal would rather have Bucky than Skattebo in a 1-for-1 that is happening in real leagues.
takes.mechanism: Feature back with goal-line role.

takes.why: Hold if he cost an 8th-9th round pick, but trade him 1-for-1 for Brian Thomas Jr., Lloyd, Harold Fannin, Quentin Johnston, Adams, Etienne or Tucker Kraft if a Colts fan is excited he's back.
takes.mechanism: 1,000 yards on 84 targets (18% share, 49th in NFL) relied on 50-yard TDs and is due for regression; Daniel Jones off a torn Achilles loses downfield arm (Cousins/Rodgers precedent); Pierce himself is off March ankle surgery and won't be 100%; more competition from Warren, Downs and Keenan Allen.

takes.why: Sal expects Warren to be the No. 1 player in the Colts' passing attack.
takes.mechanism: Daniel Jones off an Achilles favors short/intermediate throws; Pittman gone, healthy entering Week 1.

takes.why: The No. 1 player overall in the Colts offense; Sal mocks leagues trading him for Skattebo.
takes.mechanism: Team wants to run through Taylor with a QB coming off an Achilles.

takes.why: Perfect sell-high at a 7th-8th round price; swap him for Carnell Tate immediately if offered; still a potential league-winner if Mike Evans goes down.
takes.mechanism: Second-round rookie is at best the No. 3-4 option behind Evans, Deebo Samuel and Kittle (Christian Kirk hurt); ~4-6 targets a game like Jauan Jennings once everyone is healthy.

takes.why: The key Thursday-night watch: is he a full-time starter at 75%+ snaps in Week 1? Mike thinks so.
takes.mechanism: Snap share, not the box score, decides whether he's a hold.

takes.why: 'Easily' take Tate for Brooks or Stribling; go get him immediately if a Stribling-for-Tate offer exists.
takes.mechanism: Top-5 overall pick who is the No. 1 receiver in his offense; stock dipped only because he didn't catch a ball in the preseason.

takes.why: Makes no sense as a 10th-11th round pick; take a similar-range shot with a path to WR1 (e.g. Golden) instead.
takes.mechanism: Third-round rookie will never be the No. 1 option behind Zay Flowers, Bateman and Andrews on a run-first Lamar/Henry offense, camp hype notwithstanding.

takes.why: Popped in preseason and 'has looked awesome', but Andy isn't confident he plays enough snaps in Week 1 to judge.
takes.mechanism: Non-first-round rookie WRs start slow; snap share is the tell.

takes.why: 'Give me Odunze ASAP' for Lloyd, Parker Washington or Brooks.
takes.mechanism: Proven target earner in a better (Bears) offense than Jacksonville.

takes.why: Sal takes Adams over Parker Washington or Alec Pierce.
takes.mechanism: Proven receiver in the Rams offense.

takes.why: Auto-start for where you drafted him Thursday night; the watch is whether the 33-year-old looks sluggish.
takes.mechanism: Volume role in the league's best offense (30 ppg last year) vs a 49ers D ranked 26th vs WRs.

takes.why: Sal would do Lloyd for Watson.
takes.mechanism: Prefers a proven WR over an unproven RB profile.

takes.why: Lloyd-for-Harrison is a trade Sal makes.
takes.mechanism: Proven talent whose stock dipped after ARI's bottom-5 offense last year.

takes.why: Lloyd-for-Waddle: 'obviously you're doing that'.
takes.mechanism: Established WR1-level receiver.

takes.why: Someone got Garrett Wilson for Parker Washington; Sal would do it.
takes.mechanism: Proven target hog.

takes.why: Not sexy, but Sal takes Montgomery for Parker Washington or Brooks if you need RBs.
takes.mechanism: Reliable veteran lead-back touches.

takes.why: London-for-Pickens: Sal does that.
takes.mechanism: Prefers a WR with a stable QB over London with Tua.

takes.why: London-for-A.J. Brown is a trade Sal makes.
takes.mechanism: Proven WR1 now paired with Drake Maye.

takes.why: Start him, but Week 1 at Seattle is a 'very, very tough matchup' and the key watch is how he looks with Maye.
takes.mechanism: Seattle's corners shut down WRs last year; Brown was mossing Riq Woolen in joint practices.

takes.why: Obviously do London-for-Jefferson if it's available.
takes.mechanism: Elite WR1.

takes.why: Sal does Skattebo-for-Love 1-for-1.
takes.mechanism: Better RB profile than Skattebo's crowded room.

takes.why: Cardinals HC 'optimistic' Love plays Sunday vs LAC; hosts dislike that verbiage and note ankle re-injury risk would open a workload for Allgeier.
takes.mechanism: Ankle injury with an 'optimistic' tag one week out.

takes.why: People scared of the turf toe are trading Achane 1-for-1 for Skattebo; Sal takes Achane.
takes.mechanism: Elite talent, injury fear is overpriced.

takes.why: Take Flowers for Skattebo; he's the Ravens' No. 1 option.
takes.mechanism: Just returned to practice, which scared some managers.

takes.why: Burden-for-Skattebo is a deal Sal accepts on the Burden side.
takes.mechanism: Young WR in an improving Bears offense.

takes.why: Take Sutton for Brooks.
takes.mechanism: Proven target earner.

takes.why: Take Kittle for Brooks; expected to play Week 1 or 2.
takes.mechanism: Older and off a torn Achilles but a proven TE1.

takes.why: All three hosts would bench Kittle Thursday night for nearly any healthy TE: Juwan Johnson, Likely, Goedert, Henry, Schultz, Strange, Hockenson or Andrews; only Dulcich loses to him.
takes.mechanism: 'All but guaranteed' limited snaps in his first game off the Achilles vs a very good Rams defense.

takes.why: Take Godwin for Brooks.
takes.mechanism: Proven volume WR.

takes.why: Take Addison for Brooks.
takes.mechanism: Established WR2 with TD upside.

takes.why: Sal takes Fannin over Alec Pierce right now.
takes.mechanism: Big role as a rookie in Stefanski's offense last year.

takes.why: Sal would take Johnston over Alec Pierce, 'which might feel crazy'.
takes.mechanism: Healthier situation than Pierce's.
